claims.text: In 1905 the Duke of San Pedro de Galatino decided to build the hotel, originally called The Hotel Casino Alhambra Palace.

findings.quote: The story of a visionary, the Duke of San Pedro de Galatino

In 1905, over a century ago, an idealistic and romantic man fell in love with the fascinating city of Granada and decided—with all the confidence and the tenacity of a lover—to build The Hotel Casino Alhambra Palace.

claims.text: The building's 'galatea orange' hue comes from the colour of iron-rich earth and shifts with the time of day, resembling the nearby Alhambra.

findings.quote: With its unique "galatea orange" hue provided by the colour of the iron-rich earth, it shows different chromatic variations depending on the time of day, resembling the majestic Alhambra nearby.

claims.text: The exterior has a crenelated, curvilinear design likened to the walls of Avila.

findings.quote: Outwardly, its crenelated and curvilinear design has an unmistakable likeness to the Avila´s wall

claims.text: The interior is neo-Moorish, with mirrors, mosaics, muqarnas and arches.

findings.quote: the neo-Moorish style abounds with splashes of mirrors, mosaics, muqarnas and arches

claims.text: El Teatrillo, the hotel's Little Theater, stands where the duke's casino once was.

findings.quote: el Teatrillo, the “Little Theater” of the palace the place where the casino, dearly loved by the duke, once stood

claims.text: El Teatrillo's size suits chamber music, solo recitals and small performances.

findings.quote: Its size makes it ideal for chamber music, solo recitals, and small performances.

claims.text: In June 1922 the theater hosted the flamenco song contest known as the Concurso del Cante Jondo.

findings.quote: In June 1922, a flamenco song contest was held in this theater called “El concurso del cante jondo” (the contest of the deep song).

claims.text: During the Civil War the hotel became a field hospital for three years.

findings.quote: It Becomes a Field Hospital for Three Years.
Once the Civil War Was Over, the Hotel Reopened Its Doors in 1942

claims.text: Red crosses painted on the roof saved the building from aerial bombardment.

findings.quote: The Roof of the Building is Painted With Red Crosses. This Saved the Building From Aerial Bombardment.

claims.text: Since the early 1980s the duke's heirs have managed the hotel directly.

findings.quote: At the beginning of the 80s of the last century, the heirs of the duke of San Pedro de Galatino took over the management of the hotel directly

claims.text: The hotel has hosted travellers, aristocrats, royalty and artists from around the world.

findings.quote: The Hotel's Style Attracts Travellers, Aristocrats, Royalty and Artists From All Over the World Looking for a Place to Dream.
